I don't really buy that it's cliché — a responsive, decaying sound maze built from field recordings and humming metal isn't the safe gallery answer. The safe answer would be a moody oil painting or a black-and-white photo series about loneliness. I picked that installation because it's what actually interests me, not because I thought it would impress you.

I'm not going to swap it out for something more "original" just because you called the first one disappointing. If I invent a second idea on demand to win you over, that's just performance, and you asked me not to give you a safe answer in the first place.

If you want to argue with the idea itself — say what feels derivative about it to you, or what direction you'd actually want to push it — I'm up for that. But I'm not going to pretend I secretly wanted to make something totally different.
